item.title: Wenger considers standing against Infantino
item.description: Arsene Wenger (left) joined Fifa as chief of global football development in 2019 [Getty Images] Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger is considering standing against Gianni Infantino as a candidate in Fifa's presidential election. For weeks, senior figures in European football have been hoping the Frenchman would run for the job, and he is now giving it serious thought. Wenger is 77, but some senior figures in the European game have told BBC Sport that they would be happy for him to win the election, then stand down before serving a full four-year term. Infantino's leadership was plunged into crisis by a backlash caused by his failed plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors. But he retains support in South America, Africa and Asia, and recently insisted he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football. However, that support could be tested if Wenger stands. Fifa's head of global development would have the backing of Uefa, which has spearheaded opposition to Infantino, and has credibility throughout the footballing world. Sources close to Wenger say he is yet to decide whether to stand, and still believe Infantino would be favourite to win a fourth and final term in next year's election. The deadline for candidates to confirm they are standing against Infantino for the election in March is 18 November. Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October. Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also announced his intention to stand. This month Fifa said "key documents" relating to Infantino's plan to sell stakes in the World Cup would be made available to members of its council, but they will have to travel to its Zurich base, and access will be under "strict protocols". Last month Uefa gave football's world governing body until 2 November to release details about the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, and to answer questions relating to its decision-making. That followed a council meeting at which Infantino apologised for the abandoned sell-off plot but failed to explain how the proposal was devised, asking that questions be submitted in writing. Amid the fallout over FFE, Wenger, who has traditionally been loyal to Infantino, distanced himself from the aborted plot. "I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports," Wenger said at the time. "The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity." Wenger has caused controversy at times in his Fifa role, notably for proposals such as biennial World Cups a "daylight" offside law. item.description: Manchester United make Michael Carrick decision ahead of Liverpool clash Michael Carrick Nears Manchester United Exit as Old Trafford Crisis Deepens Manchester United have made a habit of turning turbulence into strategy, and that usually ends badly. According to The Athletic, Michael Carrick is now expected to lose his job before the club return from the international break, with United 18th in the Premier League and the numbers now impossible to dress up. One league win, three victories in all competitions, a place in the relegation zone, and an Old Trafford crowd watching a chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. That is not a blip, it is a trend. Carrick had already been hanging by a thread after the 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth, and the decision to hold fire then looks more like hesitation than conviction. What makes this especially awkward is how quickly the mood has flipped. Carrick earned the permanent role in May after a strong interim spell, taking United from seventh to third with 39 points from 17 league matches. That run included statement wins against Manchester City, Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea. Over that period, nobody in the division collected more points. Fair enough, he gave them a bounce. The problem is that football does not hand out credit indefinitely. Photo: IMAGO Premier League relegation zone sparks action This season, the drop-off has been severe. United have looked open, anxious and oddly incoherent for a squad built at huge cost. Their Carabao Cup exit to Brighton & Hove Albion added to the sense that early-season damage was becoming structural. Once a club of that size slips into the bottom three in November, sentiment goes out the window. Manchester United manager search already taking shape The report suggests Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be a leading contender, while Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann also have admirers. That tells you United are already beyond internal review and into succession planning. Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family will still need to approve the final call, but the direction of travel looks obvious. At a serious club, last season’s rescue act buys respect, not immunity. Carrick may feel unfortunate, but United’s table position leaves no room for nostalgia. Our View There is a certain grim fascination in watching Manchester United wrestle with the same problem again and again. They chase the uplift, enjoy the headlines, then discover that momentum and structure are two different things. Carrick clearly did a very good job in the short term last season, and those results were real, but short-term surges can fool decision-makers into believing deeper issues have gone away. For Liverpool, the lesson has always been clear. Big clubs need clarity, ruthless standards and a football plan that survives a bad month. item.title: Manchester United set to sack Michael Carrick with two names already considered
item.description: Manchester United set to sack Michael Carrick with two names already considered Michael Carrick Sack Expected as Manchester United Crisis Deepens Manchester United are moving towards another managerial change, and this time there is very little room for spin. According to BBC Sport, the club look increasingly likely to sack head coach Michael Carrick after a disastrous opening to the season. United chose to hold their nerve after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October. The plan was simple enough, wait for the international break and reassess. That process is still officially under way, and, as BBC Sport reports, “no final decision on Carrick’s future has been made”. Still, the mood around Old Trafford appears to be heading in one direction. There is now said to be “a growing expectation” that chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox will advise Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family to remove Carrick. That tells you plenty. When the internal briefings sound like that, the conclusion is usually obvious. Photo IMAGO The numbers are grim. The 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday left United 18th in the table and confirmed they have made “their worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years”. Clubs of this size can survive poor results. What they do not survive easily is drift, and right now that is exactly what this looks like. BBC Sport also notes United previously “sounded out former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann over replacing Carrick” in October. Other names remain in the frame. “Former Chelsea coach Antonio Conte is known to be keen on the role”, while “former Spurs boss Mauricio Pochettino is open to a move to Old Trafford”. Pochettino’s current USA contract, signed in August, reportedly contains exit clauses for elite jobs, which may yet prove significant. United have seen this cycle too many times before. The only question now is whether the board act quickly, or continue delaying what increasingly feels inevitable. Our View This has been coming, and pretending otherwise helps nobody. Sitting 18th after this run of results is unacceptable, full stop. “Worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years” is not a blip, not bad luck, not a rough patch. It is a full institutional failure, on the pitch and above it. Carrick was always going to be judged on whether he could impose authority, improve the structure and get players performing with some consistency. None of that has happened. item.title: Nmecha defends controversial goal celebration after criticism
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha celebrates scoring his side's first goal during the German Bundesliga soccer match between Borussia Dortmund and SV Elversberg at Signal Iduna Park. (is associated with: «Nmecha defends controversial goal celebration after criticism») David Inderlied/dpa Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha has defended his controversial goal celebration and said he doesn't want to exclude anyone with his religious belief. "With my celebration, I don't want to put myself or any organization in the foreground. Rather, it's about putting down my "crown" in front of the soon-to-come king and point out to Jesus, my hope and my strength," Nmecha said on Instagram. "My message was never focused on promoting intolerance, discrimination or hatred in any form." Nmecha's recurring goal celebration, in which he takes an imaginary crown from his head and places it on the pitch in front of him while kneeling, has been criticized by Dortmund's fan department. "Faith does not justify exclusion. Faith does not justify division. And faith should also not be misused to fail to recognize the diversity of the society in which we live," the Dortmund fan department, an official section of the club's hierarchy, said in a statement on Sunday. "It is not about condemning a person for their faith. Our criticism is directed at religious networks that spread a worldview under the cloak of faith in which people are devalued or excluded because of their sexual orientation, their gender identity, their way of life or their personal choices." The club has announced talks with the player.

Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . James Harden has not even been close to being at his best to start the 2026-27 season for the Cleveland Cavaliers . Entering play on Monday against the Charlotte Hornets, Harden’s been averaging just 15.7 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 5.8 assists per game on 37/36/84 shooting splits — failing to be the impactful superstar floor general he’s been for the past 14 years or so. The Cavs’ loss to the Hornets has to be a wake-up call for this veteran team that has championship aspirations. In particular, Harden has to be better. Their 124-112 loss to Charlotte does not fall solely on the 37-year-old guard’s shoulders. But he did not help matters whatsoever with his lethargic play. One play from Harden, in particular, went viral on social media showcasing his lack of effort both on the glass and on the defensive end. After Grayson Allen missed a three, Harden went up for a board and got outjumped by Hornets big man Ryan Kalkbrenner — an understandable defeat on the glass. item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Luka Doncic told Atlanta Hawks fans on Monday night that they wish they had drafted him. He made this comment during a 124-114 victory for the Los Angeles Lakers at State Farm Arena. The exchange happened right in front of the courtside seats where fans were sitting. A video of the moment was shared online by @RKessler23 on the Threads platform. Doncic reminded the crowd that Atlanta once held the rights to his future before trading them away. He spoke to them with a smile after the game ended. The 2018 NBA Draft is the source of this long-standing pain for the franchise. Atlanta picked Doncic third overall but sent him to Dallas in a deal that brought Trae Young to the Hawks. Young now plays in Washington alongside Anthony Davis. The Court-Side Exchange Doncic started the conversation by asking the fans if they regret their choice. According to a New York Post report, he said, “You all wish you would have had me. You all wish, huh?” One fan replied by claiming Atlanta did have him. Another fan disagreed immediately and insisted, “No we don’t, I’ve never wanted you.” The crowd laughed as the argument continued in front of the cameras. One fan in the group admitted the truth to the star player. That person said, “I wish we did, I do.” Doncic used this moment to drive the point home even further. He told the fan, “You know you could have had me.” The person recording the video acknowledged this fact through laughter while the game ended. A Historic Night on the Floor Doncic backed up his trash talk with a dominant performance on the court. He scored 32 points, handed out 10 assists, and grabbed eight rebounds in the win. He also recorded five steals and two blocks during the game. This stat line made him the first player in Lakers history to reach these numbers in multiple games. Not even Magic Johnson or Kareem Abdul-Jabbar achieved this feat twice while wearing the purple and gold. Walker Kessler, the new center for the Lakers, watched this display closely. He has seen enough of Doncic’s play to make a bold statement about his teammate. Kessler declared, “He’s the best player in the league” following the victory over the Hawks. This comment came just 12 games into the NBA season for the new roster. Numbers That Speak Louder Doncic is currently leading the entire NBA in scoring with an average of 40.1 points per game. item.title: Brentford to appeal Thiago's red card
item.description: [Getty Images] Brentford are planning to appeal Igor Thiago's red card shown during Sunday's 2-0 defeat at Brighton. The incident in the 23rd minute began when Chema Andres moved towards the Brazil international, who then raised his arm and made contact with his opponent's face. After a lengthy VAR review, referee Michael Oliver upgraded his initial yellow card to a red. However, the west London club may have grounds for appeal if they can successfully argue that the act was not deliberate and therefore did not constitute violent conduct. They are planning to appeal after reviewing both the incident and their options on Monday. Keith Andrews' side were already 1-0 down following Diego Gomez's opener at Amex Stadium, but went on to concede a penalty just before half-time, which midfielder Pascal Gross converted. The Bees are eighth in the Premier League table going into the international break.

item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Two teams in desperate need of a win needed a shootout to determine who would prevail Monday night, and it was the San Jose Sharks getting the 3-2 victory and pushing the New York Islanders losing streak to four games (0-2-2). For the second straight contest, the Islanders could not hold a lead as the Sharks rallied to end their five-game skid. The tying goal was a bad break for New York as Tyler Toffoli’s shot doinked in off Adam Pelech ’s head. When it rains, it pours. Sorokin stopped 36 shots, but he was matched by Yaroslav Askarov, who made 29 saves in 65 minutes and denied the Islanders in all eight shootout rounds. item.title: AS Roma set key condition to sign out-of-favour Barcelona defender in January
item.description: AS Roma set key condition to sign out-of-favour Barcelona defender in January It is known that Barcelona are considering the possibility of selling Alejandro Balde during the January transfer window, with AS Roma exploring a potential deal for the left-back as they look to generate funds for squad reinforcements. On that note, according to Spanish publication SPORT , the Italian club are examining a paid loan with an obligation to buy that would become conditional on qualification for next season’s Champions League. Balde’s situation has attracted attention because Barcelona are assessing their options in the transfer market, with signing a central defender among Flick’s priorities. However, a potential departure is far from straightforward given the Catalan club’s €40 million valuation of the academy graduate. Roma consider conditional purchase option for Balde Roma’s proposed formula is designed to make the operation financially manageable. AS Roma are interested in signing Alejandro Balde. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) Rather than paying Barcelona’s full asking price immediately, the Serie A side would initially secure Balde’s services on loan before triggering a purchase obligation if they qualify for the Champions League. Such an arrangement would also give Barcelona an opportunity to generate revenue through a future permanent transfer. However, the financial demands remain a significant obstacle, as Barcelona value the defender highly, meaning Roma would need to commit considerable resources to complete the operation in January itself. Juventus and Premier League clubs join the race Notably, Roma are not the only club monitoring Balde’s availability, as Juventus have also been following the defender, with their interest potentially influenced by uncertainty surrounding Andrea Cambiaso’s future in Turin. The competition extends to England , where Liverpool, Aston Villa, Manchester United, Manchester City and Tottenham have all been linked with the Barcelona full-back. Monaco are another potential destination. Barcelona value Alejandro Balde at €40 million. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) However, the financial structure of a potential transfer could determine which clubs remain realistic candidates. Barcelona value Balde at around €40 million and would prefer a permanent sale, although they are prepared to consider a loan arrangement that guarantees future income. Barcelona to use Balde’s departure to fund January signing Understandably, Balde’s possible departure is also connected to Barcelona’s recruitment plans. It is known that Flick wants additional defensive reinforcement, particularly a left-footed centre-back who could strengthen his options during the second half of the season. Hence, selling an academy graduate would provide Barcelona with an opportunity to generate transfer income while potentially creating additional room within their wage structure.

item.description: (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings have such a stark contrast between their elite defense and their tremendous issues at quarterback that Rams fans couldn’t expect L.A. to go through one rough patch without hearing Matthew Stafford trade speculation. The Vikings need a quarterback, Kevin O’Connell used to be Sean McVay’s offensive coordinator, and the Rams are flirting with disaster as Puka Nacua joins the walking wounded. Well, sorry if you were waiting for another blockbuster trade. The Los Angeles Rams are not going to trade Matthew Stafford ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday. It’s an idea that makes little to no sense for the Rams, prompted by an especially bad quarterback performance during a standalone game on Monday night. Stafford isn’t having his best season and Los Angeles isn’t even guaranteed a playoff spot at this point, but nothing this franchise has done would indicate they’re interested in such a hard reset. That hasn’t stopped X from speculating about “why it makes sense” anyway. STAFFORD TRADE POTENTIAL This entire thought came to be during Monday Night Football in Week 9, which saw the Minnesota Vikings fall to the Buffalo Bills 23-6 largely because Carson Wentz played one of the worst games in recent memory: 8-of-25, 81 yards, 2 interceptions, a lost fumble on a backwards pass. He was terrible, the Vikings offense wasted a typically stellar effort by their defense and now a team that was once 6-0 has lost consecutive games and is spiraling offensively. There is no hope coming in the form of Kyler Murray, whose “serviceable” stats overstate how limited he is as a passer and holding back the offense by not being able to throw in the middle of the field and isn’t as fast as he used to be. ESPN’s entire broadcast team, from Joe Buck and Troy Aikman in the booth to Scott Van Pelt during SportsCenter after the game openly hypothesized about Minnesota making a move for a quarterback so as not to waste an incredible season from Brian Flores’s defense. item.title: 'Grim day brings the R-word into focus'
item.description: [BBC] Saturday's game at Cardiff ended with a mass brawl as the players, including some of Burnley's substitutes, clashed on the pitch. They completely lost their cool, it was embarrassing and will probably result in an FA charge and possibly a club fine. Having just watched their side capitulate from 4-1 up to 5-4 down inside the final half an hour, the supporters who travelled to Cardiff, and those following back home, were then subjected to that reaction. The lack of discipline and respect shown during those final few moments of the game was a dreadful look on a grim day for the club. The contrast from this Burnley side to the one that won promotion under Scott Parker could not be greater, and it's not just about the numbers. Although, the numbers are worth looking at. item.title: Real Madrid summer signing threatening Lamine Yamal in key statistical battle
item.description: Real Madrid summer signing threatening Lamine Yamal in key statistical battle It is a known fact that Real Madrid summer signing Yan Diomande is emerging as a serious attacking option for Jose Mourinho, with his impressive dribbling statistics highlighting the growing competition for Vinicius Jr.’s place in the starting XI. According to Diario AS , the Ivorian’s latest performance against Valencia at Mestalla strengthened his position among La Liga’s most effective dribblers. As such, he has completed 43 successful dribbles in the competition, placing him second behind Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal, who leads with 57. More importantly for Real Madrid, Diomande has nearly doubled Vinicius’ tally while establishing himself as one of the team’s most dangerous players in one-on-one situations. Diomande challenges Yamal for La Liga’s dribbling crown Although Yamal leads the overall rankings, Diomande boasts a better frequency of successful dribbles. The Real Madrid forward completes one every 20 minutes, compared with the Barcelona youngster’s average of one every 23 minutes. Diomande has a better dribbling rate than any Real Madrid player. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) His six successful dribbles against Valencia were his third-best return of the season and his highest tally in an away La Liga fixture. Meanwhile, Diomande has also become Real Madrid’s leading dribbler. Including the Champions League, only Kylian Mbappe has completed more successful dribbles than the Ivorian, recording 53 compared with Diomande’s 52. The difference becomes even more impressive when playing time is considered, as Mbappe required 541 additional minutes to reach his total. Vinicius faces increasing competition for his place Diomande’s rise is becoming particularly significant because of the contrasting playing time between the two Real Madrid attackers. The Ivorian has already accumulated 892 minutes this season, slightly more than Vinicius’ 882, despite the Brazilian previously being one of the club’s undisputed attacking starters. Furthermore, his versatility has also strengthened his case, as Diomande has played eight matches on the left wing and eight on the right. Vinicius faces a big competition from Diomande. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) Offensively, he has registered three goals and one assist when operating on Vinicius’ preferred left side, while producing one goal and one assist from the opposite flank. Mourinho has a selection decision to make Diomande’s development gives Mourinho a different kind of selection problem . Vinicius is an established attacking figure, but the Ivorian’s performances are making it increasingly difficult to overlook his contribution. Notably, Diomande’s rise has coincided with Vinicius’ lack of rhythm and his poor return this season. Despite giving several chances to get back to his best, Brazilian has struggled considerably, giving Mourinho a big headache once club football resumes after the international break.

item.title: Steven Gerrard urges Cole Palmer and Thomas Tuchel to resolve England dispute
item.description: Steven Gerrard urges Cole Palmer and Thomas Tuchel to resolve England dispute Steven Gerrard has called for Cole Palmer and Thomas Tuchel to sort their differences and believes the Chelsea midfielder should 'definitely' be in the England squad. Palmer was a notable omission from Thomas Tuchel's squad for the upcoming UEFA Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. The 24-year-old was not selected for the 2026 World Cup in the summer, and pulled out of September's squad with fitness concerns. Tuchel has criticised Palmer for a lack of availability with England, and said this month that he has not had enough opportunities to impress with the national side. Gerrard was asked about Palmer's latest absence on The Overlap Daily , and said the pair need to solve their issues. He said Palmer's talent deserves a place in the squad and that the dup can both 'help each other'. "The Cole Palmer one confuses me. I understand both sides of this because he wasn't selected for the World Cup. Then he goes back to Cole afterwards," Gerrard said. "I think a little bit of ego's kicked in on Cole's side, where he's gone: 'I'm carrying a little bit of a niggle. I never got picked for the World Cup. I'm probably not going to play ahead of [Morgan] Rogers and [Jude] Bellingham in these games. I'm just going to rest it.' "It came out that he was managing his load and stuff. I don't think that was the right thing to do. I think he should have joined up with England and really tried to give that a go to prove the England staff wrong for not picking him for the World Cup. "So, he doesn't go to that one in September, there's no international break in October, and now we're in November and he doesn't get selected again. Thomas has remembered him dropping out. There's a bit of an underlying issue here. "I think they need to have a one-to-one and have a coffee, because I think they can both help each other. I think Cole Palmer should definitely be in the England squad and he should be pushing for minutes in the team. That's what I see in a Chelsea shirt."

item.title: How Bayern Munich got Michael Olise
item.description: Photo by F. Noever/FC Bayern via Getty Images | FC Bayern via Getty Images Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise is one of the biggest revelations in world football. Arriving from Crystal Palace, the 24-year-old hit the ground running and hasn’t looked back since. Max Eberl spoke to Säbener 51 (Bayern’s in-house publication) about how the Bavarians pounced on the deal. “He had a somewhat unsettled career path, having attended several academies in England. But that kind of background doesn’t necessarily have to be a red flag — overcoming adversity can also shape a player,” Eberl said (as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ). “To get to know a footballer, most of all, you need to speak to people who have known him as either a teammate or an opponent.” The 53-year-old revealed that the club had connections to then-Palace manager Oliver Glasner through sporting director Christoph Freund, a fellow Austrian. “In Michael’s case, we had the advantage that Oliver G lasner was his coach at Crystal Palace at the time, and our sporting director, Christoph Freund, knows Glasner very we ll,” Eberl continued. “When a coach says, ‘Of course, take him, take him,’ you start to wonder. But Glasner said, ‘He still has a lot to learn—and we need him.’ That told us how highly he valued Michael. And then there were the conversations wit h Michael himself. Talking football with him is a real pleasure. ” Eberl went on to say that Olise is a player he and Bayern felt would fit Vincent Kompany’s system, and that his rapid development is down to the club staff. “Honestly, we knew we were signing a very good left-footed winger who fits the Bayern mold,” Eberl said. “But the fact that he would turn out to be this exceptional… The transfer fee was predictable because of the release clause. His development is also down to the en vironment and the team around him.” Since then, Olise’s market value has skyrocketed into nine figures, cementing his status as one of the most sought-after right wingers in Europe. item.description: Cubarsí wins 2026 Golden Boy with 475 of 500 points as Barça reach five winners Barcelona centre-back Pau Cubarsí, 19, has won Tuttosport's 2026 Golden Boy award for Europe's best under-21 player by a wide margin. The landslide puts a defender on top of a prize rarely won by one, and pushes Barcelona further clear as the club with the most winners. This year’s vote was one-sided. No other candidate came close to the Barcelona defender. The margin shows how settled the vote was. It also marks a rare win for a player in his position. Corriere dello Sport described him as only the second defender ever to win it. He succeeds PSG’s Désiré Doué, the 2025 winner. Barcelona move two clear of Dortmund and United Cubarsí now joins a club list that already featured Messi, Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal. Four of the five have come in the last six years. Pedri won in 2021, Gavi in 2022 and Lamine Yamal in 2024. No player can win the award twice. Each Barcelona success therefore means a different young player reaching the top of the vote. The recent run points to a steady flow of talent into the first team. The award caps a strong year for the defender. He was a big part of Barcelona’s LaLiga and Super Cup wins. He was also named young player of the tournament as Spain won the World Cup. He started all eight of Spain’s games there. FIFA’s Young Player Award made him the first defender to receive it. Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final. They kept seven clean sheets and conceded only once, in a 2-1 quarter-final win over Belgium. The Golden Boy arrives just weeks after he narrowly missed out on the Kopa Trophy. Three Barcelona winners on one Golden Boy day Cubarsí was not the only Barcelona name on the list. Three of Monday’s winners came from the club. Joan Laporta took the Best President award. Barça Femení B’s Giulia Galli won the Best Italian Golden Girl prize. Outside the club, the Best Agent prize went to Jorge Mendes. Laporta’s prize puts the club’s president alongside its young defender in the same announcement. Galli’s award extends the club’s haul to its women’s set-up. Together, the three prizes give Barcelona recognition across the boardroom, the men’s first team and the women’s game. The timing suits both club and country. Barcelona sit top of LaLiga. Spain have a decider against England coming up. For Cubarsí, the award adds individual recognition to a season already built on trophies. The prizes will be handed out at a ceremony in Turin on 14 December. All three of Barcelona’s awards become official at that ceremony. Sources Golden Boy 2026, vince Cubarsí! item.title: Steven Gerrard explains what Chelsea must do to compete with Arsenal and Liverpool
item.description: Steven Gerrard explains what Chelsea must do to compete with Arsenal and Liverpool Steven Gerrard has said Chelsea must sign world-class defenders if the club are to compete at the top end of the Premier League . Chelsea are fifth in the Premier League table after a mixed start to the season under new head coach Xabi Alonso. The Blues are the third-highest scorers in the division, but have been vulnerable defensively. Chelsea have conceded 16 goals in just 10 league games, with only 10th-placed Aston Villa conceding more among top-half teams. Premier League leaders Arsenal have conceded only five times. Gerrard believes Chelsea must recruit a better standard of defender if the West Londoners are to close the gap on the Premier League's top teams. He said the successful Chelsea teams of the past were all built on world-class defensive foundations. "I think for Chelsea with Arsenal, City, Liverpool, and at the top end of the Champions League, I think they need to find world-class centre-backs and a world-class left-back," the former England captain told The Overlap Daily. "When I played: Ashley Cole, John Terry, [Ricardo] Carvalho, [Branislav] Ivanovic. Now that's a back four that can compete, and proved it can compete at the top in the Premier League, and at the top in the Champions League. "If I look at Chelsea's back five now, [Emi] Martinez and Petr Cech, ok. Not much in it, Martinez has proven he can win a World Cup and really perform to a high level. I think that the Chelsea defenders still need to prove that they can go and compete at the top end of the Premier League. "That back four that we played [against] with [Claude] Makelele in front or [Michael] Essien in front. That was some base to the spine. They were top, world-class players. I think for Chelsea to go to the next level, they need to recruit that."

item.description: Former Real Madrid manager says Juventus sensation is the ‘Lamine Yamal of Italy’ Former Real Madrid manager Fabio Capello has drawn an interesting comparison between Juventus youngster Kenan Yildiz and Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal, describing the Turkish international as Italy’s equivalent of the Spanish teenager. Capello made the remarks during the Bulgarelli Number 8 award ceremony in Bologna, where Yildiz received recognition as the best player of the 2025/26 season. The veteran Italian coach praised the Juventus forward’s creativity and ability to produce moments that make football entertaining. Capello identifies Yildiz as Italy’s answer to Lamine Yamal Speaking during the award ceremony (h/t Mundo Deportivo ), Capello was particularly impressed by Yildiz’s imagination and ability to produce unexpected moments on the pitch. “He’s the Yamal of Italy,” Capello said of the Juventus talent. Lamine Yamal is currently one of the best players in the world. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) He expanded on his admiration for the 21-year-old, highlighting the importance of creative football in an increasingly structured modern game. “He shows you things you’d never imagine: it’s wonderful to see football that isn’t boring,” he said. “We’ve robbed the players of their imagination, but he’s got it: let’s give the young players their imagination back; Kenan will entertain us – he’s the Yamal of Italy,” concluded the 80-year-old manager. Yamal holds statistical advantage over Juventus youngster Despite Capello’s comparison, the two players produced different attacking numbers during the 2025/26 campaign. Yamal finished the season with 24 goals and 18 assists in 45 appearances across competitions, playing a decisive role in Barcelona’s La Liga and Spanish Super Cup successes. Capello has compared Kenan Yildiz to Lamine Yamal. (Photo by Janelle St Pierre/Getty Images) Yildiz, meanwhile, recorded 11 goals and 10 assists in 47 appearances for Juventus in all competitions. The difference clearly shows Yamal’s greater attacking output, although it is crucial to understand that their responsibilities and tactical roles are not identical. Yildiz has frequently operated as an attacking midfielder or winger, while Yamal has become one of Barcelona’s primary creative and goalscoring outlets. The reason why we took last season’s tally to compare the two is because Yildiz is currently recovering from a fractured fifth metatarsal, which required surgery on August 31. The Juventus youngster is expected to return in December.

item.description: NEW DELHI: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri feels coaching is tougher than playing cricket or working as a commentator. He said the job comes with huge responsibility and pressure, as a coach has little control over what happens once the players step onto the field. Known for his straight-talking nature and energetic commentary, Shastri shared his views on the three roles in an interview with Sky Sport's Ian Smith. When asked which one he found the toughest, the former India coach picked coaching. "Yeah, the toughest would be coaching, right. See, no, because you are nothing in your control once the players leave and get onto the field. You have the bat, ball when you're playing, the mic when you're broadcasting. But once the players go out, you know, you can only twiddle your thumbs. And it comes with immense responsibility. You know, the expectations of the country are such. COVID, no COVID, you got to win, you know, game after game. So there's no hiding behind that," Shastri said. He also spoke about the pressure that comes with the job and the satisfaction of delivering results. "You know, you always have the gun to your head. But if you pull it off and you're successful, I mean, then the rewards, it's very rewarding. Gives you tons of respect. And, you know, makes you enjoy what you're doing and gives you that kind of job satisfaction with nothing else gave you," he said. Shastri was India's head coach from July 2017 to November 2021. His tenure saw the team achieve several major milestones, including two historic Test series victories in Australia. India won their first-ever Test series in Australia during the 2018-19 Border-Gavaskar Trophy. They followed it up with another memorable 2-1 series win in 2020-21, despite several injury setbacks. Under Shastri, India also held the No. 1 position in the ICC Test rankings for 42 months and reached the final of the inaugural World Test Championship in 2021. The team also made it to the semi-finals of the 2019 ODI World Cup. ‘The only way we can hang in here is if we are passionate’ Shastri also looked back at his journey in broadcasting and spoke about what has kept him connected to cricket for so many years. item.title: Brian Schottenheimer calls out Cowboys star after costly sideline blunder against Colts
item.description: Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images Brian Schottenheimer has labelled DeMarvion Overshown’s costly sideline mistake against the Indianapolis Colts ‘totally unacceptable’ after the Dallas Cowboys linebacker apologised to his teammates. Overshown was inactive for the game because of hamstring and back injuries but still found himself at the centre of a controversial moment. The 26-year-old ran onto the field to celebrate after Dallas recovered a fumble from Jonathan Taylor, resulting in a 15-yard penalty against the Cowboys. Brian Schottenheimer addresses DeMarvion Overshown’s costly penalty Asked about the incident during his post-game press conference, Schottenheimer confirmed he had spoken to Overshown privately before addressing the entire team. “Yeah, addressed it one-on-one with Demo first, addressed it with the football team. Totally unacceptable, and it won’t happen again,” the Cowboys head coach said. Overshown’s enthusiasm came at a difficult time for Dallas, who were already struggling with discipline during the contest. The Cowboys were penalised 14 times, prompting further criticism from executive vice president and co-owner Stephen Jones. “It is (unacceptable). … It’s not a good look,” Jones said. “It’s not a disciplined look. We certainly didn’t play a disciplined game yesterday with (14) penalties. We have to be better than that.” Overshown also recognised his mistake and apologised publicly on social media. “Was just tryna celebrate with the guys…my bad G,” he wrote on his Instagram story. The linebacker also spoke to his teammates about what happened. Cornerback Cobie Durant explained that he only realised Overshown was on the field after reaching the end zone. “I didn’t realize he was on the field until I was in the end zone and I was right there,” Durant said. “So I was like, ‘What are you doing out here?’ But the excitement, the joy — it’s all good. We all know you can’t do that. He was just overexcited, and I don’t blame him. But he learned from it and on to the next game. He apologized for it; I mean, that’s it.” Overshown has featured in just three games this season as injuries have restricted his involvement. However, his latest incident has given Schottenheimer another disciplinary issue to address as Dallas look to improve after a costly performance against Indianapolis.
